title: Talking to AI
hook: The difference between a useless answer and a great one is usually the question. Give the AI context, an example, and a clear job — and treat it as a conversation, not a vending machine.
key_points: Give context: who it's for, the goal, the tone, any constraints.
Show an example of what 'good' looks like when you can.
Ask for a specific format — a list, a table, three options, 100 words.
Iterate: refine with follow-ups instead of expecting a perfect first try.
content_html: People often try AI once, get a bland answer, and conclude it's overhyped. Usually the problem is the question. A chatbot can't read your mind — it only has the words you give it. The single biggest upgrade is context: instead of "write a post about coffee," try "write a friendly 100-word Instagram caption for a small café's new oat-milk latte, aimed at students, in a warm but not cheesy tone."
extra_html: A few habits do most of the work. Give context — who it's for, what you're trying to achieve, the tone, and any limits (length, reading level, things to avoid). Show an example of what good looks like when you have one; models are excellent at matching a pattern. Ask for a format — "give me three options," "as a table," "in plain language a beginner would get." And treat it as a back-and-forth: if the first reply misses, don't start over — say what to change. "Too formal, make it warmer" or "shorter, and add a call to action" steers it quickly. None of this requires special "prompt engineering" tricks; it's just clear communication, the same skill you'd use briefing a new assistant.

related.title: Chatbots & Assistants
related.hook: ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini feel like talking to a person, but they're generative AI with a chat wrapper — brilliant writing partners, unreliable encyclopedias.

related.title: When AI Makes Things Up
related.hook: AI 'hallucinations' aren't glitches — they're the technology working as designed. A model that always predicts a plausible next word will sometimes produce a plausible falsehood.

related.title: Common Prompting Mistakes
related.hook: Most 'AI is useless' moments trace back to a handful of fixable habits: asking too vaguely, dumping everything at once, and accepting the first draft as final.

related.title: AI for Writing
related.hook: Writing is where AI earns its keep for most people: not replacing your voice, but beating the blank page, tightening drafts, and translating 'ugh' into a sendable email.

flashcards.prompt: What most reliably improves an AI's answer?

choices.text: Giving it context, an example, and a clearly defined task
Using as few words as possible

flashcards.explanation_html: The model can't read your mind. Spelling out the audience, goal, format, and an example of 'good' is what turns vague replies into useful ones.

flashcards.prompt: If the first answer isn't quite right, what should you do?
flashcards.back_html: Treat it as a conversation — give feedback and follow-ups ("shorter," "more formal," "add an example") rather than expecting a perfect first try.
